tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Returns the universal context-setting primer for Hemrock models, plus an optional template-specific addendum. Always run this first before any other prompts.

tools.name: get_prompts
tools.description: Returns task-specific Layer 2 prompts for a given template and task type. These are ready-to-use prompts for common modeling tasks.

tools.name: get_checks
tools.description: Returns Layer 3 sanity-check and validation prompts — the 'where AI gets financial modeling wrong' guidance. Use these to audit AI-generated work or catch common modeling errors.

tools.name: get_best_practices
tools.description: Returns Hemrock's financial modeling best practices and design principles for a given topic. Useful as background context for AI interactions.

tools.name: list_concepts
tools.description: Lists Hemrock financial-modeling concept docs — the methodology behind the math (exit waterfalls, anti-dilution, convertibles, cohorts, circular references, unit economics, and more). Returns a compact index of slugs, titles, and descriptions. Optionally filter by template_name or tag. Call get_conc

tools.name: get_concept
tools.description: Returns the full text of a single Hemrock concept doc by slug. Use this to learn how a financial-modeling calculation actually works before building or auditing it. Get valid slugs from list_concepts.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: Lists the hosted Hemrock calculation engines (cap table, exit waterfall, fund economics), what each computes, and its price and checkout link. Free and needs no sign-in, so call it when the user asks what Hemrock can calculate or what it costs.

tools.name: get_access
tools.description: Returns public access terms for an engine: product, annual price, billing period, annual allowance, and a customer checkout URL. This is informational and does not purchase or confirm account-specific access; use get_account_access for the authenticated account.

tools.name: get_account_access
tools.description: Returns whether this connection is signed in, its annual product access and remaining calculations. Does not consume allowance. Call it before a compute tool if you are unsure the user can run one. If the result contains action_required (not signed in, no purchase, allowance used), relay it to the u

tools.name: get_account_usage
tools.description: Returns signed-in usage history and endpoint/source breakdown. Does not consume allowance. If the result contains action_required (not signed in, no purchase, allowance used), relay it to the user with its links and offer to retry. Never skip the calculation silently.

tools.name: cap_table_compute
tools.description: Use whenever the user asks who owns what after a financing: founder splits, option pools, priced rounds, SAFEs and convertible notes converting, warrants, pro-rata, or dilution across several rounds. tools.description: Use whenever the user asks what each holder gets at an exit, acquisition or liquidation: liquidation preferences, participating vs non-participating preferred, participation caps, seniority, whether a series converts, options and warrants in or out of the money. Takes the cap stack and an exit value

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_access · Public sink: cap_table_compute · Destructive: get_context, get_account_access.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_access · Public sink: cap_table_compute · Destructive: get_context, get_account_access

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_models" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Lists the Hemrock financial-model engines callable over the API, with pricing and (for paid ones) a checkout URL. No API key needed — use this to discover what you can run and what it costs before authenticating." → after: "Lists the hosted Hemrock calculation engines (cap table, exit waterfall, fund economics), what each computes, and its price and checkout link. Free and needs no sign-in, so call it when the user asks what Hemrock can calculate or what it costs."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
